target.title: fix #98107: Gateway regenerates service-env file on every restart, wiping Telegram bot tokens
target.body:
Closes #98107

## What Problem This Solves

macOS LaunchAgent regeneration could erase an active channel credential from the generated service-env file when the update/restart shell did not re-export that config SecretRef. The next gateway process then started without the token.

## Why This Change Was Made

The service install plan now receives the installed environment-value provenance and can retain an existing value only when all of these remain true:

- current config still references the normalized key as a SecretRef;
- the key is a safe service environment name;
- the installed value came from OpenClaw's generated file (`file` or `inline-and-file`).

The retained value is fallback-only: current state-dir dotenv, shell, and auth sources still win. Start-time stale-service repair forwards the same provenance into this one canonical plan.

Deep review found and fixed an important boundary bug in the earlier patch: filtering against all managed keys could resurrect a stale generated-file value after config moved the key to `env.vars`. The final code filters strictly against current config SecretRef keys. Retired refs, source migrations, unsafe keys, and inline-only values are dropped.

## User Impact

Gateway reinstall/update/restart no longer wipes active generated-file-backed SecretRef credentials merely because the invoking shell lacks them. Credential rotation and explicit current sources remain authoritative.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox: 49 focused tests passed (48 install-plan cases and one start-repair case).
- Regression coverage includes two active SecretRefs, retired managed keys, `env.vars` source migration, unsafe names, provenance filtering, and source precedence.
- Blacksmith Testbox: remote formatting passed for all touched files.
- Fresh full-diff autoreview: clean, confidence 0.93.
- Native review artifacts: validated, zero findings.
- Contributor live macOS proof: secret-absent LaunchAgent regeneration kept a 0600 service-env file and token equality; `launchctl` reported the temporary service active; Telegram `getMe` succeeded with the regenerated-file token; cleanup completed.

The live macOS proof was captured on the contributor pre-sync head. The current exact tree is verified by patch-continuity review plus the focused Testbox regressions above.
